identity.title: Cut Your Losses in Large-Vocabulary Language Models

problem.claim: Large-vocabulary language-model training can make cross-entropy loss computation the dominant memory cost because it constructs logits for input-token/vocabulary-item pairs.

contributions.claim: Cut Cross-Entropy (CCE) computes the correct-token logit and vocabulary-wide log-sum-exp on the fly, avoiding global materialization of all logits.
CCE uses a custom flash-memory kernel and skips gradient elements whose contributions fall below numerical precision.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present CCE as a way to make global-memory consumption for cross-entropy negligible while retaining the loss computation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that, for Gemma 2 (2B), CCE reduces loss-computation memory from 24 GB to 1 MB and classifier-head training memory from 28 GB to 1 GB.
The authors report that the memory reduction occurs without sacrificing training speed or convergence.

narrative_sequence.summary: Growing vocabularies make cross-entropy a disproportionately large training-memory consumer.
CCE avoids storing the full logit matrix by computing only the correct-token logit and reducing over vocabulary logits on the fly.
A custom kernel operates in flash memory, and negligible softmax-gradient contributions are skipped to improve throughput.
On Gemma 2 (2B), the authors report major memory reductions with no reported loss in training speed or convergence.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs a concrete memory bottleneck with an implementation mechanism and reports resource changes in absolute units for a named model.

lessons.interpretation: Resource-focused method claims become more informative when the bottleneck, mechanism, test setting, and before/after quantities are linked.
lessons.application: Frame a systems contribution by naming the dominant resource, explaining which intermediate is avoided, and reporting absolute baseline-to-method changes on a specified model.
lessons.exception: This framing is less suitable when resource usage is not the primary contribution or when absolute measurements are unavailable or incomparable.

unknowns: The abstract does not state what prior approaches or understanding constitute a specific gap.
Experimental setup, datasets, hardware, evaluation duration, and convergence criteria are unspecified.
The abstract does not provide throughput values or conditions supporting the reported speed and convergence comparison.
